## PDF page 60

[Open source PDF](../../../../sources/pdf/GTO/Poker-Math-Preflop-Workbook.pdf#page=60)

```text
                       WIDER RANGES


Let’s turn up the intensity and look at some looser starting ranges. But instead
of listing out each starting hand, which can get unwieldy with wider ranges,
we will group starting hands into usable “buckets.”

In the table below, jot down the combos for each starting hand type. Here is
how I define each of these types:

      TYPE           INCLUDES                     DESCRIPTION
  Pocket Pairs        AA or 66    Two of the same ranked card
   Unpaired        AT, KJs, QJ, JTs, Includes two Broadway cards (A, K, Q, J, T),
   Broadway            AK, etc.      suited or unsuited. Does NOT include pocket
     Hands                           pairs like KK or TT.
Straight & Flush    98s, 75s, A4s Any hand that does NOT include two
Drawing Hands                     Broadway cards that is both suited and
                                  able to flop a straight. This includes suited
                                  connectors (98s), suited gappers (97s, 96s,
                                  95s), Ace-wheel suited (A2s-A5s), etc.
     Other         T9o, A3o, Q6s All hands that do not fit into the other
                                 buckets


Once you complete the table, add up all of combos and fill in the box at
the bottom. Keep a close eye on the number of combos of pocket pairs vs.
unpaired Broadway hands in these ranges. Also notice how the “other” bucket
is impacted as the starting range goes beyond 500 combos.



                                    PA G E 6 0
```
